title: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay: Including the NSW Police Salary
description: Learn how to convert hourly pay to annual salary using a 38-hour week. Includes the NSW police salary average, tax, Medicare, and superannuation explained.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52; the NSW police salary average is $2108.80 per week (full-time ordinary time, May 2026).

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax, Medicare, and super. Remember that this assumes you work every week of the year with no unpaid leave or overtime.

faqs.q: What is the NSW police salary and how does it compare to the national average?
faqs.a: The NSW police salary is not a single figure; it varies by rank and experience. However, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time ordinary time earnings in New South Wales averaged $2108.80 per week in May 2026. This is an average across all occupations, not a median for police officers. For a police-specific figure, you would need to check the relevant award or enterprise agreement.

faqs.q: How is tax and the Medicare levy calculated on my annual pay?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income, but reduction thresholds for 2026–27 were not confirmed in this estimate; the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here. Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary, up to the $270,830 contribution base.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly Pay to Annual Salary

If you earn an hourly wage or have been offered a salary, understanding the annual equivalent helps you compare jobs and plan your budget. The standard method is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks in a year.

### The 38-Hour Week Assumption

Most full-time roles in Australia are based on a 38-hour week, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Fair Work Commission. When you see a salary figure on our [reference tables](/data) or in pay guides, we assume 38 hours unless stated otherwise. For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, which equals $1004.44 per week (38 hours) and $1004.44 × 52 = $52,231.88 per year. If you work more or fewer hours, adjust the weekly figure changes accordingly.

### Including the Fortnightly Pay

A fortnight is simply two weeks multiplied by two: weekly pay × 2. For a $30 per hour on a 38-hour week, your fortnightly gross pay is $30 × 38 × 2 = $2,280. This helps when you receive salary packaging or compare with salary packaging and super.

## Award Rates and Casual Loading

Award rates set minimum pay for specific industries. The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor. Many employees receive higher award rates based on their classification. Casual workers get a 25% casual loading on top of the base rate, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. For example, the casual minimum wage $26.44 per hour plus 25% loading = $33.05 per hour. Always check your award or enterprise agreement. Do not tell the reader to type a rate that already includes casual loading. Our [timesheet](/) home page has a checkbox to add 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base.

## Tax and Medicare on Your Annual Pay

Annual gross pay is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a $30 per hour on a 38-hour week, annual gross = $30 × 38 × 52 = $52,200. Then apply 2026–27 resident tax scale: nil to $18,200; 15% to $45,000; 30% to $135,000; 37% to $190,000; 45% above that. Medicare levy generally 2% of taxable income. The Australian Taxation Office uses the full tax-free threshold. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used for Medicare because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. No HELP, Medicare levy surcharge and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate.

## The NSW Police Salary Average

The keyword "nsw police salary" appears in the Australian Bureau of Statistics May 2026 full-time ordinary time in New South Wales: $2108.80 per week. This is an average, not a median for police officers. For a police-specific figure, check the relevant award or enterprise agreement. The average across all occupations in NSW is $2108.80 per week. The national average full-time ordinary time is $2083.70 per week. All employees total earnings $1579.20 per week includes part-time.

The [timesheet](/), [about the timesheet](/about), [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage), [take-home pay](/topics/take-home), [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging), [average pay](/topics/average-pay), [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion), [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading), [job pay](/topics/job-pay) are available.

## Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
